Why pans are compared by area

Bake time depends mostly on how deep the batter is. If two pans have the same area, the same recipe fills them to the same depth and bakes in about the same time, whatever their shape. So the converter works out the area of each pan (π × radius² for a round, length × width for the rest) and tells you how much more or less batter you need to fill yours to the same depth.

Round pans hold less than their size suggests. A 9-inch round has about the same area as an 8-inch square, and going up one inch on a round pan adds about 25% more room. That's why an 8-inch layer cake recipe looks thin in 9-inch pans.

If you don't want to scale the recipe

Within about 10% either way, the recipe works as written. Past that, the batter ends up noticeably deeper or thinner. A deeper batter needs longer in the oven, and the edges can overbake before the middle sets, so lower the temperature by 25 °F and test with a toothpick. A thinner batter bakes faster, so start checking about two thirds of the way through the time. To change the amounts, the recipe scaler multiplies every line for you.

Glass and dark pans

Glass and dark nonstick pans absorb more heat than shiny metal and brown the edges faster. Many bakers lower the oven by 25 °F when using them, especially for cakes and brownies.

Questions

Can I use a 9×13 pan instead of two 9-inch rounds?

Yes. Two 9-inch rounds hold about 127 square inches and a 9×13 holds 117, so the batter sits a little deeper in the 9×13. Use the recipe as written and expect it to need a few extra minutes.

What size round pan equals an 8×8 square?

A 9-inch round. Both are about 64 square inches, so they take the same recipe and a similar bake time.

How much more batter does a 9-inch round need than an 8-inch?

About 27% more, so multiply the recipe by 1¼. A 9-inch round is 63.6 square inches and an 8-inch round is 50.3.

How do I use a recipe written for a pan in centimeters?

Choose a custom round, square or rectangle, switch the unit to cm and enter the size. A 20 cm round is close to an 8-inch round, and a 23 cm round is close to a 9-inch.

Does pan depth matter?

The converter assumes both pans are the same depth, which is true of most cake pans (2 inches). Fill cake pans about half to two thirds full, so a deep pan with the same area doesn’t need more batter.
